  1229	We describe an honest, value-$1$ PCC strategy for the Pauli basis test.
  1230	
  1231	
  1232	\begin{lemma}\label{lem:pauli-completeness}
  1233	  The Pauli basis test $\game^\pauli_\qldparams$ has a value-$1$ SPCC strategy.
  1234	\end{lemma}
  1235	
  1236	\begin{proof}
  1237	  We begin by specifying the value-$1$ strategy $\strategy = (\ket{\psi}, E)$.
  1238	  The state is
  1239	  \begin{equation*}
  1240	    \ket{\psi} = \ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes M} \otimes \ket{\EPR_2}\;.
  1241	  \end{equation*}
  1242	  Now we specify the measurements.
  1243	  We start with measurements associated with questions of type $\Point$,
  1244	  $\ALine$, $\DLine$, and $\Pauli$.
  1245	  Using notation introduced in Section~\ref{sec:ld-encoding}, for $W \in \{X,
  1246	  Z\}$,
  1247	  \begin{align*}
  1248	    E^{(\Point,W),\, y}_{\, a}
  1249	    & = \tau^W_{[g_{\cdot}(y) = a]} \otimes I\;,\\
  1250	    E^{(\ALine,W),\, \line}_{\, f}
  1251	    & = \tau^W_{[(g_{\cdot})|_\line = f]} \otimes I\;,\\
  1252	    E^{(\DLine,W),\, \line}_{\, f}
  1253	    & = \tau^W_{[(g_{\cdot})|_\line = f]} \otimes I\;,\\    
  1254	    E^{(\Pauli,W)}_{\, a}
  1255	    & = \tau^W_{a} \otimes I\;.
  1256	  \end{align*}
  1257	  Here, the bracket notation used to post-process measurement outcomes is
  1258	  defined in \Cref{def:bracket}.
  1259	  Thus, for example, the measurement on question $((\Point,W),y)$ corresponds to
  1260	  first performing the measurement $\{\tau^W_h\}_{h \in \F_q^M}$, receiving an
  1261	  outcome $h \in \F_q^M$, and then outputting the value $a = g_{h}(y)$.
  1262	
  1263	  For $\ALine$ and $\DLine$ questions, the question content $\line$ denotes
  1264	  either an axis-parallel line $\line(u_0,e_i)$ for some $i \in
  1265	  \{1,2,\ldots,m\}$, or a diagonal line $\line(u_0,v')$ for some $v' \in
  1266	  \F_q^m$.
  1267	  As described at the beginning of \Cref{sec:qld-game}, axis-parallel lines are
  1268	  specified by pairs $(u_0,s) \in \F_q^m \times \F_q$ and diagonal lines are
  1269	  specified by triples $(u_0,s,v) \in \F_q^m \times \F_q \times \F_q^m$.
  1270	  The measurement on question $((\ALine,W),\line)$, for example, corresponds to
  1271	  first performing the measurement $\{\tau^W_h\}_{h \in \F_q^M}$ to get an
  1272	  outcome $h \in \F_q^M$, and reporting the univariate polynomial $f_\line(t) =
  1273	  g_{h}(u_0 + te_i)$ where $\line$ is specified by $(u_0,s)$ and $i = \chi(s)$.
  1274	  
  1275	
  1276	
  1277	  Next we specify the POVMs associated with questions of type $\Constraint$,
  1278	  $\Variable$, and $\Pair$.
  1279	  Questions with these question types have a question content that is a tuple
  1280	  $\omega= (u_\xpt, u_\zpt, r_\xpt, r_\zpt)\in (\F_q^m)^2 \times \F_q^2$.
  1281	  Given such a tuple, consider the two $\F_2$-valued POVMs $A=\{A_b\}_{b \in
  1282	    \F_2}$ and $B=\{B_b\}_{b \in \F_2}$ defined as
  1283	  \begin{align}
  1284	    A_b & = \tau^X_{[\tr(g_{\cdot}(u_X)\, r_\xpt) = b]} \otimes I\;,\label{eq:gonna-expand-A}\\
  1285	    B_b & = \tau^Z_{[\tr(g_{\cdot}(u_Z)\, r_\zpt) = b]} \otimes I\;.\label{eq:gonna-expand-B}
  1286	  \end{align}
  1287	  We would like to determine when the two observables $\mathcal{O}_A = A_0 -
  1288	  A_1$ and $\mathcal{O}_B = B_0 - B_1$ commute or anti-commute.
  1289	  Towards this we derive alternative expressions for these observables from
  1290	  which their commutativity becomes plain from inspection.
  1291	  We begin by inspecting the first matrices on the right-hand sides of
  1292	  Equations~\eqref{eq:gonna-expand-A} and~\eqref{eq:gonna-expand-B}:
  1293	  \begin{align}
  1294	  \tau^W_{[\tr(g_{\cdot}(u_W)\, r_W) = b]}
  1295	  &= \sum_{h : \tr(g_{h}(u_W)\, r_W) = b} \tau^W_h\nonumber\\
  1296	  &= \sum_{h : \tr((h\, \cdot\, \ind_{m}(u_W)) \cdot r_W ) = b} \tau^W_h\;,\label{eq:expand-with-dot-product}
  1297	  \end{align}
  1298	  where~\eqref{eq:expand-with-dot-product}
  1299	  follows by  Definition~\ref{eq:low-degree-encoding-definition}.
  1300	  As a result,
  1301	  \begin{align}
  1302	&  \tau^W_{[\tr(g_{\cdot}(u_W)\, r_W) = 0]}
  1303	  -   \tau^W_{[\tr(g_{\cdot}(u_W)\, r_W) = 1]} \notag \\
  1304	  & = \sum_{h : \tr((h\, \cdot\, \ind_{m}(u_W)) \cdot r_W ) = 0} \tau^W_h
  1305	  	- \sum_{h : \tr((h\, \cdot\, \ind_{m}(u_W)) \cdot r_W ) = 1} \tau^W_h\nonumber\\
  1306	  & = \sum_{h} (-1)^{\tr((h\, \cdot\, \ind_{m}(u_W)) \cdot r_W )} \tau^W_h\nonumber\\
  1307	  & = \tau^W(\ind_{m}(u_W)r_W)\;,\label{eq:finally-got-an-observable}
  1308	  \end{align}
  1309	  where the last step uses~\eqref{eq:pauli-obs-proj}.
  1310	  As a result, Equation~\eqref{eq:finally-got-an-observable}
  1311	  and Equations~\eqref{eq:gonna-expand-A} and~\eqref{eq:gonna-expand-B} imply that
  1312	  \begin{equation*}
  1313	  \mathcal{O}_A = \tau^X(\ind_{m}(u_X)r_X) \otimes I,\quad
  1314	  \mathcal{O}_B = \tau^Z(\ind_{m}(u_Z)r_Z) \otimes I\;.
  1315	  \end{equation*}
  1316	  Now, let $\gamma = \tr((\ind_{m}(u_X)r_X) \cdot (\ind_{m}(u_Z)r_Z)) \in \F_2$,
  1317	  as in Equation~\eqref{eq:gamma-value}.
  1318	  Then by Equation~\eqref{eq:twisted-fq},
  1319	  \begin{equation*}
  1320	  \mathcal{O}_A \mathcal{O}_B = (-1)^{\gamma} \mathcal{O}_B \mathcal{O}_A\;.
  1321	  \end{equation*}
  1322	  As a result, $\gamma$ quantifies whether the observables $\mathcal{O}_A$ and
  1323	  $\mathcal{O}_B$ commute, and therefore whether the measurements~$A$ and~$B$
  1324	  commute.
  1325	  If $\gamma = 0$, they commute.
  1326	  If $\gamma = 1$, they anti-commute.
  1327	  We now specify the POVMs associated with questions of type $\Constraint$,
  1328	  $\Variable$, and $\Pair$, considering separately the cases when $\gamma = 0$
  1329	  or $\gamma = 1$.
  1330	  \begin{enumerate}
  1331	  \item If $\gamma = 0$, 
  1332	     for each $\beta_X, \beta_Z \in \F_2$ define
  1333	    \begin{equation}\label{eq:pair-definition}
  1334	      E^{\Pair,\, \omega}_{\beta_X,\, \beta_Z} = A_{\beta_X} \cdot B_{\beta_Z}\;,
  1335	    \end{equation}
  1336	    \begin{equation*}
  1337	      E^{(\Pair,X),\, \omega}_{a} = A_{a} \;,\qquad
  1338	      E^{(\Pair,Z),\, \omega}_{a} = B_{a}\;.
  1339	    \end{equation*}
  1340	    The POVM associated with questions of type $\Constraint$ and $\Variable$ are
  1341	    defined to be trivial.
  1342	    In particular, we define
  1343	    \begin{equation*}
  1344	      E^{\Constraint_i,\, \omega}_{\, 0,\, 0,\, 0}
  1345	      = E^{\Variable_j,\, \omega}_{\, 0} = I\;,
  1346	    \end{equation*}
  1347	    and the remaining POVM elements in these measurements are set to be zero.
  1348	  \item If $\gamma = 1$, then $\mathcal{O}_A$ and $\mathcal{O}_B$ anti-commute.
  1349	    In this case we define measurements $E^{\Constraint_i,\, \omega}$ and
  1350	    $E^{\Variable_j,\, \omega}$, for all $i\in\{1,\ldots,6\}$ and $j
  1351	    \in\{1,\ldots,9\}$ to be those guaranteed by Theorem~\ref{thm:ms-from-ac}.
  1352	    Measurements associated with inputs of type $\Pair$ are defined to be
  1353	    trivial.
  1354	    In particular, we define
  1355	    \begin{equation*}
  1356	      E^{\Pair,\, \omega}_{0,\, 0} = E^{(\Pair,X),\, \omega}_{0} = E^{(\Pair,Z),\, \omega}_{0} = I\;,
  1357	    \end{equation*}
  1358	    and the remaining matrices in these measurements are set to be zero.
  1359	  \end{enumerate}
  1360	  This completes the specification of the strategy.
  1361	
  1362	  Now, we show that $\strategy$ is a value-$1$ SPCC strategy.
  1363	  It is clearly symmetric and projective. 
  1364	  To show that it is consistent, we note that all measurements are Pauli basis
  1365	  measurements, which are consistent, or measurements produced by
  1366	  Theorem~\ref{thm:ms-from-ac}, which are also consistent.
  1367	  The only exception is the $\Pair$ measurement in the $\gamma = 0$ case, which
  1368	  by Equation~\eqref{eq:pair-definition} is a product of two commuting,
  1369	  consistent measurements, and so it is therefore also consistent.
  1370	  To show that it is commuting, we note that for each $W \in \{X, Z\}$, all
  1371	  $(\Point, W)$, $(\ALine, W)$, $(\DLine,W)$ and $(\Pauli, W)$ measurements
  1372	  commute as they are all measurements in the Pauli~$W$ basis.
  1373	  Next, if $\gamma = 0$ then the $\Constraint$ and $\Variable$ measurements

  1380	  trivially, and the $\Constraint$ and $\Variable$ measurements commute by
  1381	  Theorem~\ref{thm:ms-from-ac}.
  1382	  Finally, the $(\Point, X)$ measurement commutes with $\Variable_1$ because

  1384	  $\Variable_5$ are $Z$-basis measurements.

  1387		Consider first the first three tests executed by the decision procedure in
  1388	  Figure~\ref{fig:decider_pauli}.

  1426	\paragraph{Soundness of the Pauli basis test.} 
  1427	We state the soundness properties of the Pauli basis test.
  1428	The following is an adaptation of the self-testing statement in~\cite[Theorem
  1429	6.4]{NW19}.
  1430	
  1431	\begin{theorem}
  1432	  \label{thm:pauli}
  1433	There exists a function 
  1434	\[\delta_{\qld}(\eps,m,d,q) = a(md)^a(\eps^b + q^{-b} + 2^{-bmd})\]
  1435	 for universal constants $a \geq 1$ and $0 < b < 1$ such that the following holds. For all admissible parameter tuples $\qldparams = (q,m,d)$ and for all strategies $\strategy = (\ket{\psi},A,B)$ for the game $\game^\pauli_\qldparams$ that succeed with probability at least $1 - \eps$, there exist local isometries $\phi_\alice: \mH_\alice \to \mH_{\alice'} \otimes \mH_{\alice''},\phi_\bob: \mH_\bob \to \mH_{\bob'} \otimes \mH_{\bob''}$ (where $\ket{\psi} \in \mH_\alice \otimes \mH_\bob$ and $\mH_{\alice''},\mH_{\bob''} \cong (\C^q)^{\otimes M}$ with $M = 2^m$) and a state $\ket{\aux} \in \mH_{\alice'} \otimes \mH_{\bob'}$ such that 
  1436	\begin{enumerate}
  1437	    \item $\left \| \phi_\alice \otimes \phi_B \ket{\psi} - \ket{\aux} \otimes \ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes M}  \right \| \leq \delta_{\qld}(\eps,m,d,q)$,
  1438	    \item Letting $\tilde{A}^x_a = \phi_A\, A^x_a \, \phi_A^\dagger$ and $\tilde{B}^y_b = \phi_B B^y_b \phi_B^\dagger$, we have for $W \in \{X,Z\}$
  1439	    \begin{gather*}
  1440	        \tilde{A}^{(\pauli,W)}_u \otimes I_{\bob'\bob''} \approx_{\delta_{\qld}} (\tau^W_u)_{\alice''} \otimes I_{\alice' \bob' \bob''} \\
  1441	        I_{\alice'\alice''} \otimes \tilde{B}^{(\pauli,W)}_u    \approx_{\delta_{\qld}} I_{\alice' \alice'' \bob'} \otimes (\tau^W_u)_{\bob''}\;,
  1442	    \end{gather*}
  1443	    where the $\approx_{\delta_{\qld}}$ statement holds with respect to the state $\ket{\aux}_{\alice'\bob'} \otimes \ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes M}_{\alice''\bob''}$ and the answer summation is over $u \in \F_q^M$.
  1444	\end{enumerate}
  1445	\end{theorem}
  1446	
  1447	We provide a proof of \Cref{thm:pauli} in \Cref{sec:qld-analysis}. 
  1448	
  1449	
  1450	The strategies described in the proof of \Cref{lem:pauli-completeness} and in the conclusion of \Cref{thm:pauli} are described in terms of qudit Pauli measurements and maximally entangled states defined over $q$-dimensional qudits. 
  1451	However, it is more convenient for our application of the Pauli basis test to
  1452	instead deal with \emph{qubits}.
  1453	In particular, we use the Pauli basis test in the ``introspection game'' of
  1454	Section~\ref{sec:introspection}, where the players are commanded to sample
  1455	questions according to a sampler $\sampler$ of a normal form verifier.
  1456	By definition of normal form verifier, $\sampler$ is a sampler over $\F_2$, and
  1457	therefore it is natural to use a test for qubit Pauli measurements.
  1458	
  1459	Since we use field sizes $q$ that are powers of $2$, Lemma~\ref{lem:pauli-binary}
  1460	shows that the conclusions of \Cref{thm:pauli} can also be described in terms of
  1461	testing for maximally entangled states over qubits and qubit Pauli measurements.
  1462	
  1463	
  1464	
  1465	
  1466	
  1467	
  1468	
  1469	\begin{corollary}
  1470	\label{cor:pauli-binary}  
  1471	There exists a function
  1472	\[\delta_{\qld}(\eps,q,m,d) = a(md)^a(\eps^b + q^{-b} + 2^{-bmd})\]
  1473	for universal constants $a \geq 1$ and $0 < b < 1$ such that the following holds. For all admissible parameter tuples $\qldparams = (q,m,d)$ and for all strategies $\strategy = (\ket{\psi},A,B)$ for the game $\game^\pauli_\qldparams$ that succeeds with probability at least $1 - \eps$, there exist local isometries $\phi_\alice: \mH_\alice \to \mH_{\alice'} \otimes \mH_{\alice''},\phi_\bob: \mH_\bob \to \mH_{\bob'} \otimes \mH_{\bob''}$ (where $\ket{\psi} \in \mH_\alice \otimes \mH_\bob$ and $\mH_{\alice''},\mH_{\bob''} \cong (\C^2)^{\otimes M \log q}$ with $M = 2^m$) and a state $\ket{\aux} \in \mH_{\alice'} \otimes \mH_{\bob'}$ such that 
  1474	\begin{enumerate}
  1475	    \item $\left \| \phi_\alice \otimes \phi_B \ket{\psi} - \ket{\aux} \otimes \ket{\EPR_2}^{\otimes M \log q}  \right \| \leq \delta_{\qld}(\eps,m,d,q)$,
  1476	    \item Letting $\tilde{A}^x_a = \phi_A\, A^x_a \, \phi_A^\dagger$ and $\tilde{B}^y_b = \phi_B B^y_b \phi_B^\dagger$, we have for $W \in \{X,Z\}$
  1477	    \begin{gather*}
  1478	        \tilde{A}^{(\pauli,W)}_u \otimes I_{\bob'\bob''} \approx_{\delta_{\qld}} (\sigma^W_u)_{\alice''} \otimes I_{\alice' \bob' \bob''} \\
  1479	        I_{\alice'\alice''} \otimes \tilde{B}^{(\pauli,W)}_u    \approx_{\delta_{\qld}} I_{\alice' \alice'' \bob'} \otimes (\sigma^W_u)_{\bob''}
  1480	    \end{gather*}
  1481	    where the $\approx_{\delta_{\qld}}$ statement holds with respect to the state $\ket{\aux}_{\alice'\bob'} \otimes \ket{\EPR_2}^{\otimes M \log q}_{\alice''\bob''}$ and the answer summation is over $u \in \F_q^M$. Here, $\sigma^W_u$ denotes the tensor product of single-qubit Pauli measurements
  1482	    \[
  1483	    	\bigotimes_{i=1}^{M} \bigotimes_{j=1}^{\log q} \sigma^W_{u_{ij}}
  1484	    \]
  1485	    where $\kappa(u_i) = (u_{ij})_{1 \leq j \leq \log q}$ (using the bijection $\kappa: \F_q \to \F_2^{\log q}$ from \Cref{sec:finite-fields}).
  1486	\end{enumerate}  
  1487	\end{corollary}
  1488	
  1489	\begin{proof}
  1490	\Cref{lem:pauli-binary} implies that there are local isometries that map $\ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes M}$ to $\ket{\EPR_2}^{\otimes M\log q}$, and map the generalized Pauli measurements $\tau^W_u$ to $\bigotimes_{i=1}^M \bigotimes_{j=1}^{\log q} \sigma^W_{u_{ij}}$ where $\kappa(u_i) = (u_{i1},\ldots,u_{i\log q})$. Combining this with the isometries guaranteed by \Cref{thm:pauli}, we obtain the statement of the Corollary.
  1491	\end{proof}
  1492	\subsubsection{Canonical parameters and complexity of the Pauli basis test}
  1493	\label{sec:qld-complexity}
  1494	
  1495	We specify a canonical setting of the parameter tuple $\qldparams$ as a function
  1496	of an integer $R$.
  1497	We call this canonical setting $\introparams$ because we use these in the
  1498	``introspection'' section (\Cref{sec:introspection}).
  1499	We then give bounds on the complexity of computing the decision procedure and CL
  1500	functions of the Pauli basis test corresponding to the parameter tuple
  1501	$\qldparams$, as a function of $R$.
  1502	
  1503	\begin{definition}[Canonical parameters of the Pauli basis test]
  1504	  \label{def:introparams}
  1505	  Let $a,b$ be the universal constants specified in Theorem~\ref{thm:pauli}.
  1506	  Let $c$ denote the smallest even integer that is at least $(b + a)/b$.
  1507	  For all integers $R \geq 4$, define the tuple $\introparams(R) = (q,m,d)$
  1508	  where
  1509	  \begin{itemize}
  1510	  	\item $q = 2^k$ for $k = c \lceil  \log \log R  \rceil + 1$.
  1511		\item $m = 2^j$ where $2^j \leq c \lceil \log R \rceil + 1 < 2^{j+1}$. 
  1512		\item $d = 1$. 
  1513	  \end{itemize}
  1514	\end{definition}
  1515	
  1516	Intuitively, this choice of parameters is such that the Pauli basis test
  1517	certifies the presence of an $M=2^m$-qudit EPR state (of local dimension $q$), or
  1518	equivalently an $M\log q$-qubit EPR state.
  1519	
  1520	\begin{lemma}
  1521	  \label{lem:delta-bound}
  1522	 For all integers $R \geq 4$, the parameter tuple $\introparams(R) = (q,m,d)$ is
  1523	  admissible (see Definition~\ref{def:admissible}), satisfies $2^m \geq R$, and furthermore there exist
  1524	  universal constants $a'\geq 1$ and $0 < b' \leq 1$ such that the function
  1525	  $\delta_\qld(\eps, m, d, q)$ from Theorem~\ref{thm:pauli} is at most
  1526	   \[
  1527	   	a' ( \log(R)^{a'} \cdot \eps^{b'} + \log(R)^{-b'}) \;.
  1528		\]
  1529	\end{lemma}
  1530	
  1531	\begin{proof}
  1532	  We verify the admissibility of $\introparams(R)$ first: the field size $q =
  1533	  2^k$ is admissible because $k$ is odd. We have $m | q$ because for all $R \geq 4$ we have  
  1534	  \[
  1535	  	2^j \leq 2 c \lceil \log R \rceil \leq 2 \log^c R \leq 2^k~.
  1536	  \]
  1537		Next, we show that $R \leq 2^m$. Since $m = 2^j \geq (c/2) \log R$, we have that
  1538		\[
  1539			2^m \geq R^{c/2} \geq R
  1540		\]
  1541		where we used that $c \geq 2$. 
  1542	
  1543	Finally, we show the desired bound on the error function $\delta_\qld(\eps,m,d,q)$. First, observe that $2^{-bmd} \leq q^{-b}$ because $k \leq m$.
  1544	  Note that for $R \geq 2$, we have $m \leq 2c \log R$, and furthermore $q =
  1545	  2^k \geq \log^c R$.
  1546	Then, we get
  1547	\begin{align*}
  1548	  	\delta_\qld(\eps,m,d,q)
  1549	    & = a (md)^a (\eps^b + q^{-b} + 2^{-bmd}) \tag{by Theorem~\ref{thm:pauli}}  \\
  1550	    & \leq a (md)^a (\eps^b + 2q^{-b}) \tag{because  $2^{-bmd} \leq q^{-b}$}  \\
  1551	    & = a (m)^a (\eps^b + 2q^{-b}) \tag{because  $d=1$}  \\
  1552	    & \leq a (2c)^a \log^{a} (R) ( \eps^{b} + 2q^{-b}) \tag{because  $m \leq 2c \log R$}\\
  1553	    & \leq a (2c)^a \log^{a} (R) ( \eps^{b} + 2(\log R)^{-cb}) \tag{because  $q \geq \log^c R$}\\
  1554	    & \leq 2a (2c)^a \log^{a} (R) ( \eps^{b} + (\log R)^{-cb}) \\
  1555	    & = 2a (2c)^a ( (\log R)^{a}\eps^{b} + (\log R)^{a-cb}) \\
  1556	    & \leq 2a(2c)^{a} \left ( (\log R)^{a} \eps^{b}
  1557	      + (\log R)^{-b} \right) \tag{because  $cb - a \geq b \geq 0$}\\
  1558	    & \leq a' ( (\log R)^{a'} \eps^{b} + (\log R)^{-b}),
  1559	  \end{align*}
  1560	  where $a'$ is defined as the quantity $2a(2c)^a$.
  1561	This completes the proof of the lemma.
  1562	\end{proof}
  1563	
  1564	\begin{lemma}
  1565		\label{lem:introparams-complexity}
  1566		Fix an integer $R \geq 4$, let $\introparams(R) = (q,m,d)$.
  1567		The integers $(q,m,d) = \introparams(R)$ can be computed in time $\polylog
  1568	  R$ when given the binary representation of $R$ as input.
  1569	\end{lemma}
  1570	\begin{proof}
  1571	  This follows from the definitions of the parameters in
  1572	  Definition~\ref{def:introparams}.
  1573	  
  1574	\end{proof}
  1575	
  1576	\begin{lemma}
  1577	  \label{lem:qld-complexity}
  1578	  Let $R \geq 4$ be an integer, and let $\introparams(R)$ denote the parameter tuple
  1579	  specified by Definition~\ref{def:introparams}.
  1580	  \begin{enumerate}
  1581		\item The time complexity of the decision procedure $\decider^\pauli$
  1582	    parameterized by $\introparams(R)$ is $\poly(R)$.
  1583		\item The time complexity of computing marginals of the CL functions $L_\tvar$
  1584	    as well as the associated factor spaces, for $\tvar \in \type^\pauli$, is
  1585	    $\polylog R$.
  1586		\item The Turing machine description of the decision procedure
  1587	    $\decider^\pauli$ parameterized by $\introparams$ can be computed from the
  1588	    binary presentation of $R$ in $\polylog (R)$ time.
  1589	  \end{enumerate}
  1590	\end{lemma}
  1591	
  1592	\begin{proof}
  1593		Finite field arithmetic over $\F_q$ can be performed in time $\polylog q$, by
  1594	  Lemma~\ref{lem:efficient_arithmetic}.
  1595	  The parameters of $\introparams(R)$, which the decision procedure
  1596	  $\decider^\pauli$ implicitly computes given $R$, can be computed in time
  1597	  $\polylog(R)$, by Lemma~\ref{lem:introparams-complexity}.
  1598	  The most expensive step in $\decider^\pauli$ is to evaluate the low-degree
  1599	  encoding $g_{a}(y)$ where $a \in \F_q^M$ and $y \in \F_q^m$, which
  1600	  takes time $\poly(M,\log q) = \poly(R)$ by \Cref{lem:ld-encoding-complexity}.
  1601		
  1602	  The complexity of computing the CL functions $L_\tvar$ for types $\tvar \in
  1603	  \type^\pauli$ is dominated by the complexity of computing the CL functions
  1604	  $L_\ALine$, $L_\DLine$, and $L_\Point$ from the classical low-degree test, which takes time
  1605	  $\poly(m, \log q) = \polylog(R)$.
  1606	
  1607	  The factor spaces of $L_\tvar$ depend only on the question type $\tvar$ (of
  1608	  which there are only constantly many), and outputting the length-$m$ indicator
  1609	  vectors of the factor spaces takes $O(m) = \polylog (R)$ time.
  1610	
  1611	  Finally, the time complexity of computing the description of $\decider^\pauli$
  1612	  from the binary representation of $R$ requires $\polylog R$ time, because the
  1613	  checks performed in the decision procedure $\decider^\pauli$ depend on
  1614	  $\introparams$ which ultimately depends on $R$; we assume that the decision
  1615	  procedure computes the parameter tuple $\introparams$ based on $R$.
  1616	  Thus the time complexity is dominated by the time to write $R$ in binary.
  1617	\end{proof}
  1618

     5	# Projective strategy setup
     6	
     7	This module records the finite-dimensional projective dilation used before
     8	the observable analysis and gives its explicit zero-padding isometries.
     9	
    10	## References
    11	
    12	The setup is `lem:projective-strategy-setup` and
    13	`def:projective-strategy-general` in

    20	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT

    22	noncomputable section
    23	
    24	/-- Embed a finite Euclidean space into an equivalently indexed space by
    25	placing its coordinates in the all-zero ancilla sector. This is the

    27	`ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:412-475`, paper
    28	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:155-172`. -/
    29	noncomputable def padWithZeros {ι κ : Type*}
    30	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] [Fintype κ] [DecidableEq κ] {n : ℕ}
    31	    (e : κ ≃ ι × (Fin n → Bool)) :
    32	    EuclideanSpace ℂ ι →ₗᵢ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ κ := by
    33	  let L : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι →ₗ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ κ :=
    34	    { toFun := fun ψ => (EuclideanSpace.equiv κ ℂ).symm fun j =>
    35	        if (e j).2 = 0 then (EuclideanSpace.equiv ι ℂ ψ) (e j).1 else 0
    36	      map_add' := by
    37	        intro ψ φ
    38	        apply (EuclideanSpace.equiv κ ℂ).injective
    39	        change (fun j => if (e j).2 = 0 then
    40	          (EuclideanSpace.equiv ι ℂ (ψ + φ)) (e j).1 else 0) = _
    41	        ext j
    42	        simp only [map_add, Pi.add_apply]
    43	        split_ifs with h <;> simp [h]
    44	      map_smul' := by
    45	        intro c ψ
    46	        apply (EuclideanSpace.equiv κ ℂ).injective
    47	        change (fun j => if (e j).2 = 0 then
    48	          (EuclideanSpace.equiv ι ℂ (c • ψ)) (e j).1 else 0) = _
    49	        ext j
    50	        simp only [map_smul, Pi.smul_apply]
    51	        split_ifs with h <;> simp [h] }
    52	  refine { toLinearMap := L, norm_map' := fun ψ => ?_ }
    53	  apply (sq_eq_sq₀ (norm_nonneg _) (norm_nonneg _)).mp
    54	  rw [EuclideanSpace.norm_sq_eq, EuclideanSpace.norm_sq_eq]
    55	  change (∑ j : κ, ‖if (e j).2 = 0 then ψ (e j).1 else 0‖ ^ 2) = _
    56	  change (∑ j : κ, (fun p : ι × (Fin n → Bool) =>
    57	    ‖if p.2 = 0 then ψ p.1 else 0‖ ^ 2) (e j)) = _
    58	  calc
    59	    _ = ∑ p : ι × (Fin n → Bool),
    60	        ‖if p.2 = 0 then ψ p.1 else 0‖ ^ 2 := e.sum_comp _
    61	    _ = _ := by
    62	      rw [Fintype.sum_prod_type]
    63	      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
    64	      intro i _
    65	      rw [Finset.sum_eq_single (0 : Fin n → Bool)]
    66	      · simp
    67	      · intro b _ hb
    68	        simp [hb]
    69	      · intro h
    70	        exact (h (Finset.mem_univ _)).elim
    71	
    72	/-- Reindex the product of two padded local spaces into the source bipartite
    73	space followed by the two ancilla spaces. This is the explicit shuffle in
    74	`lem:projective-strategy-setup`, blueprint
    75	`ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:412-475`. -/
    76	def paddedProdShuffle {ιA ιB κA κB : Type*} {nA nB : ℕ}
    77	    (eA : κA ≃ ιA × (Fin nA → Bool))
    78	    (eB : κB ≃ ιB × (Fin nB → Bool)) :
    79	    κA × κB ≃ (ιA × ιB) × ((Fin nA → Bool) × (Fin nB → Bool)) :=
    80	  (Equiv.prodCongr eA eB).trans prodShuffle
    81	
    82	/-- Every finite tensor-product strategy has an equal-value projective
    83	dilation whose state is obtained by local zero padding. This is
    84	`lem:projective-strategy-setup`, blueprint
    85	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:412-475`, paper
    86	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:155-172`.
    87	The proof route is Naimark dilation followed by residual-projector completion. -/
    88	theorem exists_projective_padded_strategy (G : Game) (S : Strategy G) :
    89	    ∃ (nA nB : ℕ) (T : Strategy G)
    90	      (eA : T.ιA ≃ S.ιA × (Fin nA → Bool))
    91	      (eB : T.ιB ≃ S.ιB × (Fin nB → Bool)),
    92	      T.IsProjective ∧
    93	        reindexState (paddedProdShuffle eA eB) T.ψ =

    96	        T.value = S.value := by
    97	  sorry
    98	
    99	end

1	\chapter{Strategy observables and the expanded space}
     2	\label{chap:qpbt-observables}
     3	% This chapter covers the first three subsections of the source appendix
     4	% ``Analysis of the Pauli basis test''
     5	% (references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex, lines 1-679).
     6	% The paper's subsection labels sec:qld-prelim, sec:commutation and
     7	% sec:expanding are kept on the sections below for cross-reference fidelity.
     8	% The source restates thm:pauli verbatim at the head of the appendix under the
     9	% label thm:pauli-appendix (lines 6-20); the statement is the same theorem, and
    10	% all references here are to thm:pauli as stated in Chapter chap:qpbt-test.
    11	
    12	This chapter and the two that follow contain the proof of the soundness
    13	theorem for the Pauli basis test, Theorem~\ref{thm:pauli}, stated in
    14	Chapter~\ref{chap:qpbt-test}. Starting from a strategy that succeeds in the
    15	game $\mathfrak{G}^{\mathrm{Pauli}}_{(q,m,d)}$ with high probability, the proof
    16	constructs a representation of the Pauli group on the players' Hilbert space
    17	in several stages. In Section~\ref{sec:commutation} the strategy measurements
    18	are used to define a set of observables that correspond to a subset of the
    19	Pauli $X$ and $Z$ observables, and these observables are shown to
    20	approximately satisfy the associated Pauli group relations. In
    21	Section~\ref{sec:expanding}, ancillary registers containing EPR states are
    22	adjoined to the players' state, and a new set of approximately commuting
    23	observables acting on the expanded state is defined.
    24	Chapter~\ref{chap:qpbt-combining} combines the approximately commuting
    25	observables into a strategy for the \emph{classical} low individual degree
    26	test and applies the soundness theorem of that test to construct a single
    27	projective measurement that simultaneously measures all of them.
    28	Chapter~\ref{chap:qpbt-extraction} uses this simultaneous measurement to
    29	construct an exact representation of the Pauli group, shows that it is close
    30	to the original strategy observables on the expanded state, and deduces
    31	Theorem~\ref{thm:pauli}. Section~\ref{sec:qld-prelim} below collects
    32	preliminary definitions and lemmas used throughout the analysis.
    33	
    34	\section{Preliminaries}
    35	\label{sec:qld-prelim}
    36	
    37	\begin{definition}[Individual and total degree polynomial classes]
    38		\label{def:ideg-deg-polynomials}
    39		\lean{MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries.polyFunc}
    40		\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.TotalDegreePoly}
    41		\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.DegPoly, MIPStarRE.QPBT.evalCoefficient}
    42		\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.DegPoly.padTo, MIPStarRE.QPBT.EvaluatesTo, MIPStarRE.QPBT.evalOpt}
    43		\leanok
    44		\uses{def:line, def:line-representative, def:polyfunc}
    45		Given integers $d, m \geq 0$ and a prime power $q$, denote by
    46		$\mathrm{ideg}_{d,m}(\F_q)$ the set of polynomials in $m$ variables over
    47		$\F_q$ with \emph{individual} degree at most $d$ in each variable. When
    48		the field is clear from context we write $\mathrm{ideg}_{d,m}$, and when
    49		the number of variables is also clear from context, $\mathrm{ideg}_d$. We
    50		denote by $\deg_d$ the set of polynomials with \emph{total} degree at
    51		most $d$.
    52		% The line-restricted classes below are introduced only implicitly in the
    53		% source, in the statement of the lemma labelled lem:qld-comm-line-cons,
    54		% which reads them as polynomials "defined on the line". The coefficient
    55		% reading adopted here follows the answer format of the decision procedure
    56		% of the low individual degree game (source figure fig:ld-decider) and the
    57		% representative convention of def:polyfunc; see the remark following this
    58		% definition.
    59		For a line $\ell \subseteq \F_q^m$ (Definition~\ref{def:line}) presented
    60		by a base point $u_0$ and a direction $v$ --- for the lines arising as
    61		question contents, the pair read off the line's description, whose base
    62		point is the canonical representative of
    63		Definition~\ref{def:line-representative} --- and an integer $c \geq 0$,
    64		we write $\deg_c(\ell)$ for the set of univariate polynomials of degree
    65		at most $c$, each given by its list of $c+1$ coefficients and identified
    66		by its polynomial representative rather than by the function it induces,
    67		as in Definition~\ref{def:polyfunc}; the argument $\ell$ records the
    68		line to which such an answer refers, through the parameterization
    69		$t \mapsto u_0 + tv$. The cases used below are $\deg_d(\ell)$ and
    70		$\deg_{md}(\ell)$; whenever $d \leq md$, extending coefficient lists by
    71		zeros gives the inclusion $\deg_d(\ell) \subseteq \deg_{md}(\ell)$. For
    72		$f \in \deg_c(\ell)$, $u \in \ell$, and $a \in \F_q$, we say that $f$
    73		\emph{evaluates to $a$ at $u$}, written $f(u) = a$, if $f(t) = a$ for
    74		every $t \in \F_q$ with $u = u_0 + tv$. When $v \neq 0$ this $t$ is
    75		unique, so every $f$ evaluates at every point of $\ell$; when $v = 0$,
    76		so that $\ell = \{u_0\}$, exactly those $f$ that induce a constant
    77		function on $\F_q$ evaluate at $u_0$, to their constant value. An
    78		operator indexed by $f(u)$ is understood to be the zero operator when
    79		$f$ does not evaluate at $u$, and for a family $\{N_f\}$ indexed by
    80		$f \in \deg_c(\ell)$ we write
    81		$N_{[\mathrm{eval}_u(\cdot)=a]} = \sum_{f \colon f(u) = a} N_f$; when
    82		$v = 0$ the classes indexed by $a \in \F_q$ form a sub-measurement
    83		rather than a partition of the outcomes. The \emph{completed} family of
    84		evaluation classes is the family indexed by $a \in \F_q \cup \{\bot\}$
    85		obtained by adjoining the additional class
    86		$N_{[\mathrm{eval}_u(\cdot)=\bot]} = \sum_{f} N_f$, the sum over those
    87		$f$ that do not evaluate at $u$; when $\{N_f\}$ is a POVM,
    88		respectively a projective measurement, the completed classes form one
    89		as well, and when $v \neq 0$ the class
    90		$N_{[\mathrm{eval}_u(\cdot)=\bot]}$ is the zero operator.
    91	\end{definition}
    92	
    93	\begin{remark}[Line answers as coefficient lists]
    94		\label{rem:deg-line-representatives}
    95		The source refers to the elements of $\deg_{md}(\ell)$ as polynomials
    96		``defined on the line $\ell$'', that is, as functions on the point set
    97		of $\ell$, while its decision procedure expects each line answer as a
    98		list of coefficients. The two readings differ. When $md \geq q$,
    99		distinct coefficient lists induce the same function $\F_q \to \F_q$;
   100		and when $\ell$ has direction $v = 0$ --- a case the question
   101		distributions produce with positive probability
   102		(Remark~\ref{rem:ld-win-zero-direction}) --- the point set of $\ell$ is
   103		the singleton $\{u_0\}$, so a function on $\ell$ retains only a single
   104		field element of the answer. Definition~\ref{def:ideg-deg-polynomials}
   105		therefore adopts the coefficient reading, under which the strategy's
   106		line measurements are indexed by exactly the answers of the prescribed
   107		form, and its evaluation convention reproduces the universal
   108		quantification of the line-versus-point clauses of the win predicates
   109		(Definition~\ref{def:ld-win-predicate}).
   110	\end{remark}
   111	
   112	Throughout this chapter $q = 2^k$ with $k$ odd is an admissible field size
   113	(Definition~\ref{def:admissible-size}) and $M = 2^m$ is the number of
   114	$q$-ary qudits tested for per player, as in
   115	Chapters~\ref{chap:qpbt-test} and~\ref{chap:qpbt-extraction}. (The letter
   116	$M$ also denotes the measurement operators of the strategy under analysis,
   117	as in the tuple $\mathcal{S} = (\ket{\psi}, M)$ below and in the
   118	super- and subscripted individual operators such as
   119	$M^{(\mathrm{Point},W),u}_a$; the meaning is determined by context, as in
   120	the source.) Recall from
   121	Chapter~\ref{chap:qpbt-algebra} the low-degree code
   122	(see Definition~\ref{def:low-degree-encoding}), which maps each vector
   123	$h \in \F_q^{M}$, with
   124	coordinates indexed by binary strings of length $m$, to a polynomial
   125	$g_h \in \mathrm{ideg}_{d,m}(\F_q)$ such that $g_h(u) = h_u$ for every
   126	$u \in \{0,1\}^m$; for $x \in \F_q^m$ the associated vector
   127	$\mathrm{ind}_m(x) \in \F_q^{M}$ satisfies
   128	$g_h(x) = h \cdot \mathrm{ind}_m(x)$ for all $h$. Recall also the finite
   129	field trace $\tr = \tr_{q \to 2} \colon \F_q \to \F_2$
   130	(see Definition~\ref{def:subfield-trace}).
   131	
   132	\begin{definition}[Commuting and anticommuting tuples]
   133		\label{def:anticommuting-tuple}
   134		\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliTuple}
   135		\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.IsAnticommuting, MIPStarRE.QPBT.IsCommuting}
   136		\leanok
   137		% The quantity gamma is introduced in the source at eq:gamma-value, inside
   138		% the completeness analysis of the Pauli basis test; the definition below
   139		% is self-contained and does not depend on that occurrence.
   140		\uses{def:low-degree-encoding, def:subfield-trace}
   141		For a tuple
   142		$\omega = (u_X, u_Z, r_X, r_Z) \in (\F_q^m)^2 \times (\F_q)^2$, let
   143		\[
   144			\gamma(\omega) \,=\, \tr\big( (r_X \cdot \mathrm{ind}_m(u_X)) \cdot (r_Z \cdot \mathrm{ind}_m(u_Z)) \big)\,,
   145		\]
   146		where $r_W \cdot \mathrm{ind}_m(u_W)$ is the scalar multiple of the
   147		vector $\mathrm{ind}_m(u_W) \in \F_q^{M}$, the middle $\cdot$ is the
   148		$\F_q$-inner product of two vectors in $\F_q^{M}$, and
   149		$\tr = \tr_{q \to 2}$. The tuple $\omega$ is called \emph{anticommuting}
   150		if $\gamma(\omega) \neq 0$, and \emph{commuting} if $\gamma(\omega) = 0$.
   151	\end{definition}
   152	
   153	The sign $(-1)^{\gamma(\omega)}$ is exactly the sign with which the
   154	generalized Pauli observables $\tau^X(r_X \cdot \mathrm{ind}_m(u_X))$ and
   155	$\tau^Z(r_Z \cdot \mathrm{ind}_m(u_Z))$ commute
   156	(see Lemma~\ref{lem:twisted-commutation});
   157	this is the source of the terminology.
   158	
   159	\begin{lemma}[Probability of anticommuting tuples]
   160		\label{fact:omega-anticomm-prob}
   161		\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.anticommProb, MIPStarRE.QPBT.anticommProb_eq}
   162		\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.commProb, MIPStarRE.QPBT.commProb_ge_half}
   163		\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.anticommProb_ge_of_m_le_q}
   164		\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.anticommProb_ge_of_one_le_md}
   165		\leanok
   166		% The source states this result in a `fact' environment; it is stated here
   167		% as a lemma, and the paper label is kept verbatim.
   168		% The exact value of the anticommuting probability and the constant lower
   169		% bounds under the hypothesis m <= q are additions relative to the source,
   170		% which asserts only the two bounds displayed at the end of the statement;
   171		% the source states those bounds without the hypothesis m, d >= 1, under
   172		% which alone they hold (see the remark following this lemma). The
   173		% unconditional constant bounds are what the proof of the lemma labelled
   174		% lem:qld-win-implications uses.
   175		\uses{def:anticommuting-tuple}
   176		A tuple $\omega = (u_X,u_Z,r_X,r_Z)$ sampled uniformly at random from
   177		$(\F_q^m)^2 \times (\F_q)^2$ is anticommuting with probability exactly
   178		\[
   179			\big(1 - q^{-1}\big)^{m+1} \cdot \frac{1}{2}\,,
   180		\]
   181		and commuting with the complementary probability, which is at least
   182		$\frac12$. In particular, if $m \leq q$, then $\omega$ is anticommuting
   183		with probability at least $2^{-4}$ and commuting with probability at
   184		least $\frac12$. If $m, d \geq 1$, then the probability that $\omega$ is
   185		anticommuting is at least
   186		\[
   187			(1 - q^{-m}) \cdot (1 - q^{-1}) \cdot \Big(1 - \frac{md}{q}\Big) \cdot \frac{1}{2}
   188			\,\geq\, \Big(1 - \frac{3md}{q}\Big) \cdot \frac{1}{2}\,,
   189		\]
   190		and the probability that $\omega$ is commuting is also at least
   191		$\big(1 - \frac{3md}{q}\big) \cdot \frac{1}{2}$.
   192	\end{lemma}
   193	\begin{proof}
   194		\uses{def:low-degree-encoding, def:indicator-vector, def:admissible-size, def:binary-representation, lem:downsize_field, lem:one}
   195		By the definition of the indicator vector
   196		(Definition~\ref{def:indicator-vector}), expanding the product over the
   197		coordinates $i \in \{1, \dots, m\}$ into a sum over $y \in \{0,1\}^m$
   198		gives
   199		\[
   200			\mathrm{ind}_m(u_X) \cdot \mathrm{ind}_m(u_Z)
   201			\,=\, \sum_{y \in \{0,1\}^m} \mathrm{ind}_{m,y}(u_X)\, \mathrm{ind}_{m,y}(u_Z)
   202			\,=\, \prod_{i=1}^{m} \big( u_{X,i}\, u_{Z,i} + (1 - u_{X,i})(1 - u_{Z,i}) \big)\,,
   203		\]
   204		and since $\F_q$ has characteristic $2$, the $i$-th factor equals
   205		$1 + u_{X,i} + u_{Z,i}$. Hence
   206		\[
   207			\gamma(\omega) \,=\, \tr\Big( (r_X r_Z) \cdot \prod_{i=1}^{m} (1 + u_{X,i} + u_{Z,i}) \Big)\,.
   208		\]
   209		For any fixed $u_X$, the $m$ factors $1 + u_{X,i} + u_{Z,i}$ are
   210		independent and uniformly distributed in $\F_q$ over the choice of
   211		$u_Z$, so all of them are nonzero with probability $(1-q^{-1})^m$;
   212		independently, $r_X \neq 0$ with probability $1 - q^{-1}$. If $r_X = 0$
   213		or some factor vanishes, then $\gamma(\omega) = 0$. Otherwise, over the
   214		uniform choice of $r_Z$, the argument of the trace is a uniformly random
   215		element of $\F_q$. Since $q = 2^k$ is admissible, the trace of an
   216		element of $\F_q$ equals the coordinate sum of its binary
   217		representation: writing $\kappa$ for the binary representation with
   218		respect to the fixed self-dual normal basis
   219		(Definition~\ref{def:binary-representation}), item~2 of
   220		Lemma~\ref{lem:downsize_field} gives
   221		$\tr(c) = \tr(c \cdot 1) = \kappa(c) \cdot \kappa(1)$, and $\kappa(1)$
   222		is the all-ones vector by Lemma~\ref{lem:one}. As $\kappa$ is a
   223		bijection onto $\F_2^k$, a uniformly random element of $\F_q$ has trace
   224		$0$ with probability exactly $\frac12$. Combining, the probability that
   225		$\gamma(\omega) \neq 0$ is exactly $(1-q^{-1})^{m+1} \cdot \frac12$, and
   226		the probability that $\omega$ is commuting is the complement, which is
   227		at least $\frac12$.
   228	
   229		If $m \leq q$, then
   230		$(1-q^{-1})^{m+1} \geq (1-q^{-1})^{q+1} = (1-q^{-1})^{q} \cdot (1-q^{-1})$,
   231		a product of two positive functions of $q$ that are nondecreasing for
   232		$q \geq 2$, so it is minimized at $q = 2$, where it equals $2^{-3}$;
   233		hence the anticommuting probability is at least $2^{-4}$.
   234	
   235		Finally, suppose $m, d \geq 1$, and consider the first inequality of
   236		the display, which bounds the anticommuting probability from below.
   237		If $md > q$, that lower bound is negative --- it is the product of
   238		the positive factors $1 - q^{-m}$, $1 - q^{-1}$, and $\frac12$ with
   239		the negative factor $1 - md/q$ --- so the anticommuting probability,
   240		being nonnegative, exceeds it. If $md \leq q$, then by Bernoulli's
   241		inequality
   242		$(1-q^{-1})^{m} \geq 1 - m/q \geq 1 - md/q \geq (1-q^{-m})(1-md/q)$,
   243		where the last step multiplies the nonnegative quantity $1 - md/q$
   244		by $1 - q^{-m} \leq 1$; multiplying by $1 - q^{-1}$ shows that the
   245		anticommuting probability is at least the first displayed bound. For
   246		the second inequality of the display, expanding the product shows
   247		that $(1-q^{-m})(1-q^{-1})(1-md/q)$ exceeds
   248		$1 - q^{-m} - q^{-1} - md/q$ by
   249		$q^{-m-1} + \frac{md}{q} \big( q^{-m} + q^{-1} - q^{-m-1} \big)$,
   250		a sum of nonnegative terms whatever the sign of $1 - md/q$; since
   251		$md \geq 1$ gives $q^{-m} \leq q^{-1} \leq md/q$, the product is
   252		therefore at least $1 - 3md/q$.
   253		The commuting probability is at least
   254		$\frac12 \geq \big(1 - \frac{3md}{q}\big) \cdot \frac12$.
   255	\end{proof}
   256	
   257	\begin{remark}[Source correction: the anticommuting probability]
   258		\label{rem:omega-anticomm-prob-correction}
   259		In the source, the statement corresponding to
   260		Lemma~\ref{fact:omega-anticomm-prob} asserts only the two bounds of the
   261		final display, without the hypothesis $m, d \geq 1$, and its proof
   262		begins with the claims that $\mathrm{ind}_m(u_X)$ vanishes if and only
   263		if $u_X = 0$ and that $u_X = 0$ forces $\omega$ to be commuting. Both
   264		claims are incorrect: the coordinates of $\mathrm{ind}_m(u)$ sum to $1$
   265		for every $u \in \F_q^m$, so $\mathrm{ind}_m(u)$ never vanishes, and for
   266		$(q,m,d) = (2,1,0)$ the tuple $\omega = (0,0,1,1)$ is anticommuting.
   267		For $d = 0$ the bounds themselves fail: with $(q,m,d) = (2,1,0)$ ---
   268		a tuple with admissible field size and $m \mid q$, excluded from
   269		Definition~\ref{def:admissible} only by the requirement $d \geq 1$
   270		that the source leaves implicit --- the exact anticommuting
   271		probability
   272		$(1-q^{-1})^{m+1} \cdot \frac12 = \frac18$ is smaller than the claimed
   273		lower bound $\big(1 - \frac{3md}{q}\big) \cdot \frac12 = \frac12$. The
   274		proof given above therefore computes the probability exactly, using the
   275		characteristic-two product formula for
   276		$\mathrm{ind}_m(u_X) \cdot \mathrm{ind}_m(u_Z)$, in place of the
   277		source's argument via the Schwartz--Zippel lemma; the exact value also
   278		supplies the unconditional constant lower bounds used in the proof of
   279		Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-win-implications}.
   280	\end{remark}

   282	\begin{definition}[Closeness of question-indexed operators]
   283		\label{def:approx-question-indexed-operators}
   284		\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.opDistSq}
   285		\leanok
   286		\uses{def:povm-distance}
   287		Let $\{A^x\}$ and $\{B^x\}$ be families of operators (not necessarily
   288		POVM elements) indexed by questions $x \in \mathcal{X}$ but not by
   289		answers, let $\mu$ be a distribution over $\mathcal{X}$, and let
   290		$\ket{\psi}$ be a state, both fixed by context. Write
   291		$A^x \approx_\delta B^x$ to denote
   292		\[
   293			\E_{x \sim \mu} \bra{\psi} (A^x - B^x)^\dagger (A^x - B^x) \ket{\psi} \,\leq\, O(\delta)\,.
   294		\]
   295		This extends the answer-indexed closeness of
   296		Definition~\ref{def:povm-distance} to answer-free families of operators,
   297		such as observables; as there, the right-hand side allows a hidden
   298		universal constant.
   299	\end{definition}
   300	
   301	The following two lemmas relate the closeness between sets of operators and
   302	weighted sums of those operators.
   303	
   304	\begin{lemma}
   305		\label{lem:avg-closeness}
   306		\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.avg_closeness}
   307		\leanok
   308		\uses{def:approx-question-indexed-operators}
   309		Let $\{A^x\}$ and $\{B^x\}$ be operators indexed by a finite set
   310		$\mathcal{X}$, let $\mu$ be a probability distribution over
   311		$\mathcal{X}$, and let $\{\alpha_x\}$ be complex numbers with
   312		$|\alpha_x| \leq 1$. If $A^x \approx_\delta B^x$ on average over
   313		$x \sim \mu$, then $A \approx_\delta B$ for the single operators
   314		$A = \E_{x} \alpha_x A^x$ and $B = \E_{x} \alpha_x B^x$, regarded as
   315		indexed by a one-element question set; quantitatively,
   316		% The closeness of Definition def:approx-question-indexed-operators
   317		% carries a hidden universal constant on both sides; the quantitative
   318		% sentence records the constant-free inequality the proof establishes.
   319		\[
   320			\big\| (A - B) \ket{\psi} \big\|^2

   416	\paragraph{The strategy under analysis.}
   417	For the remainder of this chapter, as well as in
   418	Chapters~\ref{chap:qpbt-combining} and~\ref{chap:qpbt-extraction}, we fix
   419	an admissible parameter tuple $(q,m,d)$
   420	(Definition~\ref{def:admissible}) and a strategy
   421	$\mathcal{S} = (\ket{\psi}, M)$ for the game
   422	$\mathfrak{G}^{\mathrm{Pauli}}_{(q,m,d)}$ that succeeds with probability
   423	at least $1 - \eps$, for some $\eps \geq 0$, where $\ket{\psi}$ is a
   424	bipartite state on registers $\mathsf{A}$ and $\mathsf{B}$ with associated
   425	Hilbert spaces $\hilb_{\mathsf{A}}$ and $\hilb_{\mathsf{B}}$. The symbol
   426	$M$ denotes the measurement operators of both players; which player is
   427	meant is indicated by the register on which the operator acts (for
   428	example, $M^{(\mathrm{Point},W),u}_a \ot \Id_{\mathsf{B}}$ indicates that
   429	$M^{(\mathrm{Point},W),u}_a$ is viewed as an operator acting on register
   430	$\mathsf{A}$).

   432	The analysis requires the measurements of $\mathcal{S}$ to be projective;
   433	the following lemma shows that this may be assumed without loss of

   436	\begin{lemma}[Reduction to a projective strategy]
   437		\label{lem:projective-strategy-setup}
   438		\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.exists_projective_padded_strategy}
   439		\leanok
   440		\uses{def:admissible, def:pauli-question-distribution, def:pauli-win-predicate, def:tensor-product-strategy, def:tensor-product-value, def:projective-strategy-general}
   441		Let $(q,m,d)$ be an admissible parameter tuple
   442		(Definition~\ref{def:admissible}) and let
   443		$\mathcal{S} = (\ket{\psi}, M)$ be a strategy for the game
   444		$\mathfrak{G}^{\mathrm{Pauli}}_{(q,m,d)}$, where $\ket{\psi}$ is a
   445		bipartite state on registers $\mathsf{A}$ and $\mathsf{B}$. Then there
   446		exists a projective strategy
   447		(Definition~\ref{def:projective-strategy-general}) for
   448		$\mathfrak{G}^{\mathrm{Pauli}}_{(q,m,d)}$ whose success probability
   449		equals that of $\mathcal{S}$ and whose state is the extension
   450		\[
   451			(\ket{\psi} \ot \ket{0\cdots 0} \ot \ket{0\cdots 0})_{\mathsf{A}\mathsf{B}}
   452		\]
   453		of $\ket{\psi}$ by finitely many ancilla qubits initialized in the
   454		state $\ket{0}$, adjoined to each of the two registers.
   455	\end{lemma}
   456	\begin{proof}
   457		\uses{thm:naimark, def:tensor-product-value, def:tensor-product-strategy}
   458		Naimark's theorem (Theorem~\ref{thm:naimark}), applied with the
   459		families of all of the first player's measurements on register
   460		$\mathsf{A}$ and all of the second player's on register $\mathsf{B}$,
   461		yields an auxiliary space and a projective sub-measurement replacing
   462		each family on each register, together with a product auxiliary state,
   463		such that every correlation
   464		$\bra{\psi} M^{x}_a \ot M^{y}_b \ket{\psi}$ of $\mathcal{S}$ is
   465		reproduced on the extended state. Each auxiliary space embeds into a
   466		register of finitely many qubits; extend each dilated sub-measurement
   467		to the enlarged register by adding to one fixed outcome both the
   468		projector onto the orthogonal complement of the embedded subspace and
   469		the residual projector of the sub-measurement. The outcome operators
   470		remain mutually orthogonal projectors, now summing to the identity,
   471		and no correlation changes: the complement projector annihilates the
   472		extended state, which is supported in the embedded subspace, and so
   473		does each residual projector, because for each question pair the
   474		reproduced correlations sum to one --- the original families being
   475		POVMs (Definition~\ref{def:tensor-product-strategy}) --- which forces
   476		the projector $\Id$ minus the sum of each dilated sub-measurement to
   477		have zero mass on the extended state. Finally, since the auxiliary
   478		state is a product state, a unitary acting on each player's ancilla
   479		qubits alone carries it to $\ket{0 \cdots 0} \ot \ket{0 \cdots 0}$;
   480		conjugating the projective measurements by the same unitaries
   481		preserves projectivity and all correlations. The success probability
   482		of a strategy is a linear combination of its correlations, weighted by
   483		the question distribution and the win predicate
   484		(Definition~\ref{def:tensor-product-value}), and is therefore
   485		unchanged.
   486	\end{proof}

   800	\section{Expanding the Hilbert space and defining commuting observables}
   801	\label{sec:expanding}
   802	
   803	The next step of the analysis adjoins ancillary EPR registers to the
   804	players' state and lifts the strategy observables and measurements to the
   805	expanded state. The point of the construction is that the ancilla factor of
   806	each lifted observable carries the \emph{exact} Pauli commutation sign, so
   807	that the signs cancel and the lifted observables approximately commute for
   808	every tuple $\omega$.
   809	
   810	\begin{definition}[Expanded state]
   811		\label{def:expanded-state}
   812		\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.SixReg, MIPStarRE.QPBT.ProjectiveSetting.psiHat}
   813		\leanok
   814		\uses{lem:projective-strategy-setup, def:EPR}
   815		Recall that $M = 2^m$. Introduce registers $\mathsf{A}', \mathsf{A}'',
   816		\mathsf{B}', \mathsf{B}''$, each with Hilbert space isomorphic to
   817		$(\C^q)^{\ot M}$, and define the state
   818		\begin{equation}\label{eq:def-psihat}
   819			\ket{\hat{\psi}}_{\mathsf{A}\mathsf{A}'\mathsf{A}''\mathsf{B}\mathsf{B}'\mathsf{B}''}
   820			\,=\, (\ket{\psi})_{\mathsf{A}\mathsf{B}}
   821			\ot \ket{\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\ot M}_{\mathsf{A}'\mathsf{A}''}
   822			\ot \ket{\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\ot M}_{\mathsf{B}'\mathsf{B}''}\,,
   823		\end{equation}
   824		where $\ket{\psi}$ is the extended strategy state of the strategy
   825		under analysis (Lemma~\ref{lem:projective-strategy-setup} and the
   826		convention following it) and
   827		$\ket{\mathrm{EPR}_q}$ is the maximally entangled state on
   828		$\C^q \ot \C^q$ (Definition~\ref{def:EPR}). For the remainder of this
   829		chapter, as well as in Chapters~\ref{chap:qpbt-combining}
   830		and~\ref{chap:qpbt-extraction}, all approximations $\approx$ and
   831		$\simeq$ are evaluated with respect to the state $\ket{\hat{\psi}}$,
   832		unless stated otherwise.
   833	\end{definition}

+import MIPStarRE.QPBT.Games.StrategyClasses
+import MIPStarRE.QPBT.Observables.LineDefs
+import MIPStarRE.QPBT.Test.PauliBasisTest
+
+/-!
+# Typed strategy measurements and point observables
+
+This file fixes a projective, possibly heterogeneous strategy for the Pauli
+basis test and extracts the typed measurement families used in the analysis.
+Malformed answers are folded into a fixed valid answer, so the extracted
+families remain complete measurements. The winning hypothesis bounds their
+original wrong-form mass by the rejection probability. `Option` is used only
+for the completed line-evaluation classes.
+
+## References
+
+The ambient strategy convention and the observable `W^r(u)` are in
+`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:160-190`,
+corresponding to `def:strategy-observables` in
+`blueprint/src/chapter/ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:480-503`. The typed question
+and answer forms come from `def:pauli-question-distribution` and
+`def:pauli-win-predicate`, paper
+`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1225`
+and blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:310-392`.
+-/
+
+open scoped BigOperators Matrix ComplexOrder
+
+namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
+
+open MIPStarRE.LDT MIPStarRE.Quantum
+
+noncomputable section
+
+/-- The two local registers of a heterogeneous bipartite strategy. This is
+formalization-only indexing for the player-dependent notation at paper
+`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:160-190`. -/
+inductive PlayerSide where
+  | alice
+  | bob
+  deriving DecidableEq, Repr, Inhabited, Fintype
+
+/-- A projective strategy satisfying the winning premise used throughout
+Section `sec:commutation`. The structure retains the distinct player spaces and
+measurement families of `Strategy`. Paper
+`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:160-172`; blueprint
+`ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:385-475`. -/
+structure ProjectiveSetting (P : AdmissibleParams) (ε : ℝ) where
+  toStrategy : Strategy (pauliBasisTest P)
+  isProjective : toStrategy.IsProjective
+  win : 1 - ε ≤ toStrategy.value
+
+namespace ProjectiveSetting
+
+variable {P : AdmissibleParams} {ε : ℝ}
+
+/-- The local Hilbert-space index type on a specified player side. It indexes
+the side-qualified operators at paper
+`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:174-190`. -/
+def LocalSpace (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) : PlayerSide → Type
+  | .alice => S.toStrategy.ιA
+  | .bob => S.toStrategy.ιB
+
+instance localSpaceFintype (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (side : PlayerSide) :
+    Fintype (S.LocalSpace side) := by
+  cases side <;> simp only [LocalSpace] <;> infer_instance
+
+instance localSpaceDecidableEq (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (side : PlayerSide) :
+    DecidableEq (S.LocalSpace side) := by
+  cases side <;> simp only [LocalSpace] <;> infer_instance
+
+/-- Select the strategy measurement before outcome postprocessing on one
+player side. This is the heterogeneous interpretation of the shared symbol `M` at
+paper `14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:160-184`. -/
+def strategyMeasurement (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (side : PlayerSide)
+    (question : PauliQuestion P) :
+    Measurement (PauliAnswer P) (S.LocalSpace side) := by
+  cases side with
+  | alice => exact S.toStrategy.A question
+  | bob => exact S.toStrategy.B question
+
+/-- Embed a point into the full Pauli question space in basis `W`. This is the
+point-question content from `def:pauli-question-distribution`, paper
+`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:997-1008`, blueprint
+`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:310-354`. -/
+def contentOfPoint (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
+    (u : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) : PauliSpace P :=
+  embedLd P W fun i =>
+    match i with
+    | .inl (.inl j) => u j
+    | .inl (.inr _) => 0
+    | .inr _ => 0
+
+/-- Embed a canonical line description into the full Pauli question space.
+Axis lines clear the direction block, whereas diagonal lines retain their
+canonical projected direction. Paper
+`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:997-1008`; blueprint
+`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:310-354` and `rem:deg-line-representatives`. -/
+def contentOfLine (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
+    (line : LineDesc P.toLdParams) : PauliSpace P :=
+  embedLd P W fun i =>
+    match i with
+    | .inl (.inl j) => line.base j
+    | .inl (.inr _) => line.seed
+    | .inr j =>
+        match line with
+        | .axis _ _ _ => 0
+        | .diagonal _ _ direction _ _ => direction j
+
+/-- Fill the point, scalar, and phase blocks shared by Pair, Pair/W, and Magic
+Square questions. This is the type-4 content of
+`def:pauli-question-distribution`, paper
+`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1030-1120`, blueprint
+`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:310-354`. -/
+def contentOfTuple (P : AdmissibleParams)
+    (uX uZ : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) (rX rZ : PauliScalar P) : PauliSpace P :=
+  fun i =>
+    match i with
+    | .inl (.inl (.inl (.inl (.inl j)))) => uX j
+    | .inl (.inl (.inl (.inl (.inr j)))) => uZ j
+    | .inl (.inl (.inl (.inr _))) => 0
+    | .inl (.inl (.inr _)) => 0
+    | .inl (.inr _) => rX
+    | .inr _ => rZ
+
+/-- The typed point question in basis `W`, from the strategy notation at paper
+`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:174-190` and
+`def:pauli-question-distribution`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:310-354`. -/
+def pointQuestion (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
+    (u : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) : PauliQuestion P :=
+  (.point W, contentOfPoint P W u)
+
+/-- The typed axis or diagonal line question represented by a canonical
+`LineDesc`. Paper `14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:174-184`; blueprint
+`def:strategy-observables` and `rem:deg-line-representatives`. -/
+def lineQuestion (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
+    (line : LineDesc P.toLdParams) : PauliQuestion P :=
+  match line.kind with
+  | .axis => (.aline W, contentOfLine P W line)
+  | .diagonal => (.dline W, contentOfLine P W line)
+
+/-- The typed Pair question for a tuple `(u_X,u_Z,r_X,r_Z)`. Paper
+`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:210-249`; blueprint
+`lem:qld-win-implications`. -/
+def pairQuestion (P : AdmissibleParams)
+    (uX uZ : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) (rX rZ : PauliScalar P) : PauliQuestion P :=
+  (.pair, contentOfTuple P uX uZ rX rZ)
+
+/-- The typed Pair/W question for a tuple `(u_X,u_Z,r_X,r_Z)`. Paper
+`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:210-249`; blueprint
+`lem:qld-win-implications`. -/
+def pairWQuestion (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
+    (uX uZ : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) (rX rZ : PauliScalar P) : PauliQuestion P :=
+  (.pairW W, contentOfTuple P uX uZ rX rZ)
+
+/-- The typed Magic Square question for a tuple `(u_X,u_Z,r_X,r_Z)`. Paper
+`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:213-258`; blueprint
+`lem:qld-win-implications`. -/
+def msQuestion (P : AdmissibleParams) (t : MsType)
+    (uX uZ : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) (rX rZ : PauliScalar P) : PauliQuestion P :=
+  (.ms t, contentOfTuple P uX uZ rX rZ)
+
+/-- A typed question occurs in the Pauli-test distribution when it appears on
+at least one side of a supported question pair. This Lean-only predicate makes
+the support guarantees for the question embeddings precise; blueprint
+`def:pauli-question-distribution`, `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:310-354`, paper
+`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`. -/
+def QuestionAppearsInSupport (P : AdmissibleParams) (question : PauliQuestion P) : Prop :=
+  ∃ other : PauliQuestion P,
+    (question, other) ∈ (pauliQuestionDistribution P).support ∨
+      (other, question) ∈ (pauliQuestionDistribution P).support
+
+/-- Point embeddings occur in the typed Pauli question support. This is the
+support well-formedness companion to `def:pauli-question-distribution`,
+blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:310-354`, paper
+`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:997-1008`. -/
+theorem pointQuestion_appears_in_support (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
+    (u : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) :
+    QuestionAppearsInSupport P (pointQuestion P W u) := by
+  sorry
+
+/-- Canonical axis and diagonal line embeddings occur in the typed Pauli
+question support. This is the line companion to
+`def:pauli-question-distribution`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:310-354`,
+paper `08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:997-1008`. -/
+theorem lineQuestion_appears_in_support (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
+    (line : LineDesc P.toLdParams) :
+    QuestionAppearsInSupport P (lineQuestion P W line) := by
+  sorry
+
+/-- Pair embeddings occur in the typed Pauli question support. This is the
+Pair companion to `def:pauli-question-distribution`, blueprint
+`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:310-354`, paper
+`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1030-1057`. -/
+theorem pairQuestion_appears_in_support (P : AdmissibleParams)
+    (uX uZ : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) (rX rZ : PauliScalar P) :
+    QuestionAppearsInSupport P (pairQuestion P uX uZ rX rZ) := by
+  sorry
+
+/-- Pair/W embeddings occur in the typed Pauli question support. This is the
+Pair/W companion to `def:pauli-question-distribution`, blueprint
+`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:310-354`, paper
+`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1030-1057`. -/
+theorem pairWQuestion_appears_in_support (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
+    (uX uZ : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) (rX rZ : PauliScalar P) :
+    QuestionAppearsInSupport P (pairWQuestion P W uX uZ rX rZ) := by
+  sorry
+
+/-- Magic Square embeddings occur in the typed Pauli question support. This is
+the Magic Square companion to `def:pauli-question-distribution`, blueprint
+`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:310-354`, paper
+`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1059-1120`. -/
+theorem msQuestion_appears_in_support (P : AdmissibleParams) (t : MsType)
+    (uX uZ : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) (rX rZ : PauliScalar P) :
+    QuestionAppearsInSupport P (msQuestion P t uX uZ rX rZ) := by
+  sorry
+
+/-- Pauli/W embeddings occur in the typed Pauli question support. This is the
+zero-content companion to `def:pauli-question-distribution`, blueprint
+`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:310-354`, paper
+`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1006-1008`. -/
+theorem pauliQuestion_appears_in_support (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind) :
+    QuestionAppearsInSupport P (MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauliQuestion P W) := by
+  sorry
+
+/-- Fold every non-point answer into the fixed point answer `0`. This realizes
+the typed point family without adding a bottom outcome; wrong-form mass remains
+visible through `wrongFormEffect`. Paper
+`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:174-190`; blueprint
+`def:strategy-observables`. -/
+def pointAnswerOrZero {P : AdmissibleParams} : PauliAnswer P → PauliScalar P
+  | .value a => a
+  | _ => 0
+
+/-- Fold every answer not prescribed for `line` into the zero coefficient
+list. Axis answers are padded from degree `d` to degree `m*d`. This realizes
+the coefficient convention of `def:ideg-deg-polynomials`, paper
+`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:51-62`, blueprint
+`ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:51-118`. -/
+def lineAnswerOrZero (P : AdmissibleParams) (line : LineDesc P.toLdParams) :
+    PauliAnswer P → DegPoly P.toLdParams (P.m * P.d) :=
+  match line with
+  | .axis _ _ _ => fun answer =>
+      match answer with
+      | .alinePoly f =>
+          DegPoly.padTo (Nat.le_mul_of_pos_left P.d (Nat.zero_lt_of_lt P.one_le_m)) f
+      | _ => 0
+  | .diagonal _ _ _ _ _ => fun answer =>
+      match answer with
+      | .dlinePoly f => f
+      | _ => 0
+
+/-- Fold every non-Pair answer into `(0,0)`. This is the complete typed Pair
+family used in items 4 and 6 of `lem:qld-win-implications`, paper
+`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:210-258`. -/
+def pairAnswerOrZero {P : AdmissibleParams} : PauliAnswer P → ZMod 2 × ZMod 2
+  | .pairBits bits => bits
+  | _ => (0, 0)
+
+/-- Fold every non-Pair/W answer into bit `0`. This is the complete typed
+Pair/W family used in items 4 and 7 of `lem:qld-win-implications`, paper
+`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:210-263`. -/
+def pairWAnswerOrZero {P : AdmissibleParams} : PauliAnswer P → ZMod 2
+  | .bit bit => bit
+  | _ => 0
+
+/-- Fold wrong-form Pauli-test answers into a fixed valid Magic Square answer
+of the requested question type. This supplies the typed families needed for an
+actual `Strategy msGame`; paper
+`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:213-258`, blueprint
+`lem:qld-win-implications`. -/
+def msAnswerOrZero {P : AdmissibleParams} (t : MsType) : PauliAnswer P → MsAnswer :=
+  match t with
+  | .constraint _ => fun answer =>
+      match answer with
+      | .msTriple bits => .triple bits
+      | _ => .triple 0
+  | .var _ => fun answer =>
+      match answer with
+      | .bit bit => .bit bit
+      | _ => .bit 0
+
+/-- The complete typed point measurement on one player side. It is the
+corresponding strategy measurement postprocessed by `pointAnswerOrZero`; paper
+`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:174-190`, blueprint
+`def:strategy-observables`. -/
+noncomputable def pointMeas (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (side : PlayerSide)
+    (W : PauliKind) (u : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) :
+    Measurement (PauliScalar P) (S.LocalSpace side) :=
+  (S.strategyMeasurement side (pointQuestion P W u)).postprocess pointAnswerOrZero
+
+/-- The complete typed line measurement on one player side, uniformly indexed
+by degree-`m*d` coefficient lists. Paper
+`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:174-184`; blueprint
+`def:ideg-deg-polynomials` and `lem:qld-win-implications`. -/
+noncomputable def lineMeas (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (side : PlayerSide)
+    (W : PauliKind) (line : LineDesc P.toLdParams) :
+    Measurement (DegPoly P.toLdParams (P.m * P.d)) (S.LocalSpace side) :=
+  (S.strategyMeasurement side (lineQuestion P W line)).postprocess
+    (lineAnswerOrZero P line)
+
+/-- The completed evaluation classes of a typed line measurement. This is the
+only strategy-side family whose outcome uses `Option`; `none` is precisely the
+non-evaluating class of `def:ideg-deg-polynomials`, paper
+`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:51-62`, blueprint
+`ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:51-118`. -/
+noncomputable def lineEvalMeas (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (side : PlayerSide)
+    (W : PauliKind) (line : LineDesc P.toLdParams)
+    (u : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) :
+    Measurement (Option (PauliScalar P)) (S.LocalSpace side) :=
+  (S.lineMeas side W line).postprocess (evalOpt line u)
+
+/-- The complete typed Pair measurement on one player side. Paper
+`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:210-249`; blueprint
+`lem:qld-win-implications`. -/
+noncomputable def pairMeas (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (side : PlayerSide)
+    (uX uZ : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) (rX rZ : PauliScalar P) :
+    Measurement (ZMod 2 × ZMod 2) (S.LocalSpace side) :=
+  (S.strategyMeasurement side (pairQuestion P uX uZ rX rZ)).postprocess pairAnswerOrZero
+
+/-- The complete typed Pair/W measurement on one player side. Paper
+`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:210-263`; blueprint
+`lem:qld-win-implications`. -/
+noncomputable def pairWMeas (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (side : PlayerSide)
+    (W : PauliKind) (uX uZ : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)
+    (rX rZ : PauliScalar P) : Measurement (ZMod 2) (S.LocalSpace side) :=
+  (S.strategyMeasurement side (pairWQuestion P W uX uZ rX rZ)).postprocess
+    pairWAnswerOrZero
+
+/-- The complete typed Pauli/W measurement on one player side. Paper
+`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:205-209`; blueprint
+`lem:qld-win-implications`. -/
+noncomputable def pauliMeas (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (side : PlayerSide)
+    (W : PauliKind) : Measurement (PauliRegister P) (S.LocalSpace side) :=
+  (S.strategyMeasurement side (pauliQuestion P W)).postprocess pauliAnswerOrZero
+
+/-- The complete typed Magic Square measurement on one player side. Its answer
+alphabet is exactly `MsAnswer`; these families therefore define a Magic Square
+strategy. Paper `14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:213-258`;
+blueprint `lem:qld-win-implications`. -/
+noncomputable def msMeas (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (side : PlayerSide)
+    (t : MsType) (uX uZ : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)
+    (rX rZ : PauliScalar P) : Measurement MsAnswer (S.LocalSpace side) :=
+  (S.strategyMeasurement side (msQuestion P t uX uZ rX rZ)).postprocess
+    (msAnswerOrZero t)
+
+/-- The sum of effects corresponding to answers that are invalid for a given
+question type. This mass is kept separate from the fixed valid outcome into
+which typed postprocessing folds it. Paper
+`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`, blueprint
+`def:pauli-win-predicate`. -/
+noncomputable def wrongFormEffect {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
+    (t : PauliType) (M : Measurement (PauliAnswer P) ι) : Op ι :=
+  ∑ answer ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun answer => validPauliAnswer t answer = false),
+    M.effect answer
+
+/-- The average state-dependent wrong-form answer mass for one player. Since
+the Pauli-test predicate rejects every wrong-form answer, the winning premise
+bounds this quantity. Paper
+`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`, used at paper
+`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:197-266`; blueprint
+`lem:qld-win-implications`. -/
+noncomputable def wrongFormMass (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (side : PlayerSide) : ℝ :=
+  avgOver (pauliQuestionDistribution P) fun questions =>
+    match side with
+    | .alice =>
+        (inner ℂ S.toStrategy.ψ
+          (applyOperatorToState
+            (heteroKron
+              (wrongFormEffect questions.1.1 (S.toStrategy.A questions.1)) 1)
+            S.toStrategy.ψ)).re
+    | .bob =>
+        (inner ℂ S.toStrategy.ψ
+          (applyOperatorToState
+            (heteroKron 1
+              (wrongFormEffect questions.2.1 (S.toStrategy.B questions.2)))
+            S.toStrategy.ψ)).re
+
+/-- The Alice-side wrong-form mass is at most the strategy's rejection
+probability. Paper `08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`, used at
+`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:197-266`. -/
+theorem wrongFormMass_alice_le_error (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) :
+    S.wrongFormMass .alice ≤ ε := by
+  sorry
+
+/-- The Bob-side wrong-form mass is at most the strategy's rejection
+probability. Paper `08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`, used at
+`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:197-266`. -/
+theorem wrongFormMass_bob_le_error (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) :
+    S.wrongFormMass .bob ≤ ε := by
+  sorry
+
+/-- The side-indexed strategy observable
+`W^r(u) = sum_a (-1)^(tr(ar)) M_a^((Point,W),u)`. It uses the canonical
+character `phaseSign` and the fixed trace of `P.model`. This is
+`def:strategy-observables`, paper
+`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:174-190`, blueprint
+`ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:480-503`. -/
+noncomputable def pointObs (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (side : PlayerSide)
+    (W : PauliKind) (r : PauliScalar P) (u : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) :
+    Op (S.LocalSpace side) :=
+  ∑ a : PauliScalar P,
+    phaseSign (fixedBinTrace P.model (a * r)) • (S.pointMeas side W u).effect a
+
+/-- The point observable squares to the identity. This is the assertion that
+the operator in `def:strategy-observables` has eigenvalues in `{+1,-1}`;
+paper `14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:174-190`, blueprint
+`ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:480-503`. -/
+theorem pointObs_sq_eq_one (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (side : PlayerSide)
+    (W : PauliKind) (r : PauliScalar P) (u : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) :
+    S.pointObs side W r u * S.pointObs side W r u = 1 := by
+  sorry
+
+/-- The point observable is Hermitian. This is the self-adjoint part of the
+observable assertion following `eq:qld-strat-obs`, paper
+`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:174-190`, blueprint
+`def:strategy-observables`. -/
+theorem pointObs_isHermitian (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (side : PlayerSide)
+    (W : PauliKind) (r : PauliScalar P) (u : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) :
+    (S.pointObs side W r u).IsHermitian := by
+  sorry
+
+end ProjectiveSetting
+
+end
+
+end MIPStarRE.QPBT
